title: SDK CI/CD release templates and gated checks
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the canonical CI/CD templates, gated checks, and release validation steps used by Redwood SDK teams (JS, Python, Java, Go). It is intended for SDK owners, release engineers, and developer-experience (DevX) maintainers. The goal is to ensure safe, observable, and repeatable SDK releases that preserve API compatibility and surface regressions early.

Audience and intent
- Primary: SDK maintainers, DevX engineers.
- Secondary: product owners, SRE, support.
- Intent: Provide a low-friction, high-safety pipeline template that can be copied into individual SDK repos with minimal modification.

Key guarantees (SLOs)
- Release pipeline mean time to green for PRs targeting releases: < 30 minutes for unit/integration checks.
- Compatibility assurance: canonical compatibility tests must pass on 100% of supported API variants before a major/minor SDK bump.
- Distribution success: automated publish step must succeed without manual intervention >= 95% of the time.

What this doc contains
1) Branching and versioning policy
2) Required CI checks (gated) and optional checks
3) Ready-to-use GitHub Actions templates (examples for npm/pypi/maven)
4) Release checklist and rollback steps
5) Canary and post-release monitoring
6) Ownership and runbook links

1) Branching and versioning policy
- Branch model
  - main: always deployable, contains latest stable SDK code.
  - develop (optional): integration branch for ongoing work if repo prefers trunk isolation.
  - release/x.y: short-lived branches for packaging a minor/major release.
- Versioning
  - Follow semver (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).
  - Patch: bugfixes, doc fixes.
  - Minor: new non-breaking features and improvements.
  - Major: breaking API changes — must be coordinated with API/product and require a migration guide and cross-team release window.
- Tagging convention
  - Use annotated tags: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (e.g., v1.12.3).
  - Include build metadata for CI artifacts when helpful: v1.12.3+build.20250610.

2) Required CI checks (these are GATED; PR cannot be merged until all succeed)
- Static checks (fast)
  - Linting (eslint/flake8/checkstyle) with repo-specific config.
  - License header and legal check (scancode or licencee).
- Unit tests (fast)
  - Coverage threshold: >= 60% for new code areas; target > 80% overall for mature SDKs.
- Integration tests (parallelizable)
  - Canonical API smoke tests that exercise: auth, streaming, embeddings, and error-handling paths.
  - Run against the Redwood staging environment (redwood-staging, see ENV below).
- Contract/compatibility tests (required for minor/major releases)
  - Backwards compatibility runner: run the SDK test suite against the last two released server model variants (e.g., hosted-v1 and hosted-v2).
  - Schema checks for request/response shapes using the shared openapi-schema repo.
- Packaging and artifact checks
  - Build verification: produce package and verify installability in a clean container.
  - Signature verification: ensure artifacts are signed (GPG/PGP) when configured.
- Security scans (optional gating depending on criticality)
  - Dependabot/OSS vulnerability check; fail on critical/high CVEs affecting runtime.

Fast-failure policy
- Prioritize checks so PR authors get quick feedback. Lints and unit tests should run within the first 10 minutes; longer integration/compat tests can run in parallel and be required for merge but should be reported progressively.

3) Example GitHub Actions templates
- Shared inputs (set as repo secrets/environment variables)
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY (read-only key for staging smoke tests)
  - REDWOOD_ENV (redwood-staging or redwood-dev)
  - PYPI_TOKEN / NPM_TOKEN / MAVEN_CENTRAL_TOKEN
  - SIGNING_KEY (base64-encoded for artifact signing)

- Minimal publish workflow (npm example)
```yaml
name: Release - npm
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'
jobs:
  build-and-publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '18'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - name: Install & Build
        run: npm ci && npm run build
      - name: Run smoke tests against staging
        env:
          REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}
          REDWOOD_ENV: 'redwood-staging'
        run: npm run smoke:staging
      - name: Publish to npm
        if: success()
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: npm publish --access public
```

- Packaging checklist for Python (publish to PyPI)
  - Build wheel and sdist: `python -m build`
  - Verify install in ephemeral venv: `pip install dist/*.whl`
  - Run staged smoke tests against REDWOOD_STAGING endpoint.
  - Twine upload guarded by GPG signature: `twine upload --sign --non-interactive dist/*`

4) Release checklist (copyable template)
- Pre-release (owner responsibility)
  1. Ensure CHANGELOG.md updated with links to related issues and migration steps.
  2. Confirm compatibility tests pass against the two most recent server variants.
  3. Confirm security scans and dependency updates are addressed.
  4. Verify examples and snippets in `examples/` run against staging.
  5. Update SDK docs site with release notes draft.
- Release (automation with human gate)
  1. Create release/x.y branch (if applicable) and open PR to main.
  2. Merge PR when all gated checks are green.
  3. Tag release with annotated tag `vX.Y.Z`.
  4. CI triggers release workflow and publishes artifacts.
  5. CI posts release link to #sdk-releases and creates release notes in the releases page.
- Post-release validation (first 24h)
  1. Run canary client script that exercises critical flows every 5 minutes for 24 hours.
  2. Watch telemetry: SDK error rate, install/download counts, and latency against staging-to-prod comparison.
  3. Run a smoke sample of top-downstream customers if opt-in (see customer opt-in policy).

Rollback and hotfix process
- If a release shows critical regressions (errors causing >1% error budget burn on calls from official examples or >5% regression in canary prompt success):
  1. Open an incident (see oncall_and_incident_response/incident-process) and notify #sdk-oncall and #sre.
  2. Unpublish the artifact if platform allows (npm supports deprecate/unpublish within time window); otherwise publish a patch release (vX.Y.Z+1) with fix.
  3. If unpublish is not possible, add a top-level README note and pin docs examples to previous stable tag.

5) Canary and post-release monitoring
- Canary runner
  - A small scheduled job (deployed as a GitHub Action or k8s CronJob) that runs the official `canary/` client scripts.
  - Sample checks: authentication, basic generation, streaming resume, embeddings hash stability.
- Metrics to monitor (dashboard templates exist in eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts)
  - SDK build/publish success rate (percentage of publish pipelines that succeed without manual retry).
  - Canary error rate (threshold alert: > 0.5% sustained error for 30 minutes).
  - Downloads/install rate drop (if > 30% drop relative to moving baseline alert #product).

6) Ownership and runbooks
- Owners
  - SDK repo owner: primary on-call for releases.
  - DevX Platform: owner of shared GH Action templates and release automation.
  - SRE: owner of canary infrastructure and post-release production monitors.
- Runbooks/links
  - Incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
  - Publishing keys and token rotation: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth
  - Dashboard templates: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/sdk-release-health

Appendix A — CI job matrix examples
- Example matrix for testing Node versions and runtime combos (GitHub Actions snippet):
```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    node: [16, 18, 20]
    featureFlag: [default, optin-streaming]
```
- Example matrix for Python: 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and CPython/PyPy when supported.

Appendix B — Compatibility test harness
- The canonical runner uses the shared `redwood-infra/openapi-safety` tooling to validate request/response shapes. Steps:
  1. Check out openapi-spec repo.
  2. Run `pytest tests/compatibility --env hosted-previous,hosted-current`.
  3. Fail if any breaking schema changes are detected or if >2% of canonical prompts change their pass/fail outcome.

Appendix C — Common failure modes and remediation
- Failure: Flaky smoke tests against staging because of transient auth errors.
  - Remediation: Add retry with exponential backoff; increase staging key rate limit for CI.
- Failure: Packaging fails due to missing generated code.
  - Remediation: Add a pre-build generation step and cache generation artifacts in CI.
- Failure: Post-release increase in client errors not seen in staging
  - Remediation: Capture failing request bodies and run them in a local repro harness; coordinate rollback if critical.

Copy-and-paste templates and sample checklists
- Minimal PR checklist (add to PR template):
  - [ ] Tests added/updated for new behavior
  - [ ] Linter checks green
  - [ ] Compatibility tests ran against `hosted-current`
  - [ ] Example snippet verified in `examples/`
  - [ ] CHANGELOG entry present

- Release owner contact template (in PR description):
  - Release owner: @github-username
  - Target release: vX.Y.Z
  - Compat test run id: 12345
  - Security review PR: #678

Support and escalation
- If support receives reports referencing broken examples or SDK regressions:
  1. Triage and reproduce using reproducible example in `support/` folder.
  2. If reproduction succeeds, open a high-priority issue and tag `sdk-release-regression` and `urgent`.
  3. Contact release owner and DevX oncall.

Appendix D — Migration guides and documentation hygiene
- Major releases must include:
  - Migration guide in `docs/migration/` with code diffs and suggested upgrade paths.
  - Automated codemod script (where feasible) and test coverage for codemod.
  - Deprecation warnings in minor releases prior to breaking major.

Notes and change history
- 2024-03-12: Created by Asha Patel — baseline policy and templates.
- 2024-11-18: Added compatibility thresholds and canary runner guidance (reviewers Marcus Kim).
- 2025-06-10: Expanded publish workflow examples for Java/Maven and clarified rollback steps (reviewers Eva González, Jordan Lee).

If you are adopting these templates: copy `ci-templates/` into your repo and open a short PR to DevX for a quick review. For assistance, ping #devx-help or open a ticket in the DevX board (project: DEVX-SDK).
